recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的紅血球一端拉長成單一尖尾，呈淚滴狀（dacrocyte），且在視野中數量多、方向不一，並伴隨輕度大小不均與少數棘狀紅血球；病史為骨髓纖維化。
features: Numerous red cells with a single tapered tail at one pole (teardrop cells, dacrocytes), tails pointing in random directions
Mild anisocytosis and poikilocytosis; many cells retain central pallor
Occasional crenated cells (echinocytes) and a few fragmented forms
Scattered small platelets; no nucleated cells in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows moderate poikilocytosis with numerous teardrop-shaped red cells (dacrocytes) having single tapered tails oriented in varying directions. There is mild anisocytosis with occasional echinocytes; platelets are present in small numbers. No nucleated red cells or immature myeloid cells are seen in this field, so a leukoerythroblastic picture cannot be assessed here. Findings are consistent with numerous dacrocytes, suggestive of marrow fibrosis or other infiltrative marrow process in the appropriate clinical setting.

ddx.vs: Artifactual tails all point in the same direction along the smear axis, whereas true dacrocytes here have tails oriented randomly.
Schistocytes are fragments with sharp angular edges (helmet, triangle) and lack central pallor, unlike intact teardrop cells with one rounded end.
Elliptocytes are symmetric oval or pencil shapes with both ends rounded, not a single tapered pole.
These may show some dacrocytes but also target cells, basophilic stippling or macro-ovalocytes with hypersegmented neutrophils; clinical data and marrow biopsy separate them from myelofibrosis.
